Subject: Request: updated subprocessor roster + caching SLA exception

Hi Sofia,

We are starting a compliance review ahead of our November production cutover and need the following from Redwood:

- The most recent subprocessor roster (including country/jurisdiction and whether the processor handles EU-origin data)
- Any planned subprocessor changes in the next 90 days
- Confirmation whether your caching/edge telemetry provider routes any EU customer content outside the EU (even transiently)
- If so, we need proposed mitigations and whether a DPA addendum would be required for an onshore routing carve-out or SLA exception

Can you get this to us by COB Monday (11/13)? Procurement would like a short summary PDF and a CSV roster we can ingest. Also share any links to audited evidence (SOC2 scope for the processors, KMS/HSM attestation) if available.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if easier.

Martin

Hi Martin — thanks for the heads up.

Short answers up front: we are attaching the current roster (CSV) and a one-page summary. High-level notes:

- Most processors that handle EU-origin customer data are EU or UK based.
- Our caching/edge telemetry partner (EdgeFlow) operates regional POPs; by default EU traffic is routed to EU POPs, but there are specific flows (failover and origin fetches) that may transit via non-EU infrastructure for a short period.
- We can offer an onshore routing configuration for Dedicated/Private customers or add a DPA exhibit to enumerate routing guarantees.

Attachments: subprocessor_roster_20281109.csv (CSV), subprocessor-summary-20281109.pdf (one-page).

Clarifying Qs so we can scope the ask:
1) Is FinVault asking for a global roster filter (all processors with ANY EU access) or only those that will process FinVault tenant data?
2) Do you need live traffic flow proofs (network egress snapshots) or attestations (KMS/SOC2 references) attached to the roster?

If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the roster and the proposed onshore carve-out. Ben can cover technical routing and Kimberly can speak to DPA language.

Proposed times: Fri 11/10 09:30–10:00 PT or 14:00–14:30 PT. Which works?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova

Martin / Laura — following our call and internal review, a few clarifications and proposed next steps from Redwood legal/compliance: 

1) Scope of roster: we will produce a filtered CSV showing only processors that have the FinVault tenant flag set (column: finvault_scope = true). Expect v1 by EOD Monday 11/13.

2) EdgeFlow routing: EdgeFlow is regional by default. The transient non-EU transit Martin referenced occurs only for:
   - origin fetches when the EU POP cannot reach the origin directly (failover)
   - short-lived health checks from our global controller
We have an egress map attached that highlights the flow. Mitigations we can offer immediately:
   - enable EU-only origin fetch routing for your tenant (no non-EU egress)
   - opt into Dedicated/Private with onshore-only POPs if you require an SLA-backed routing guarantee

3) DPA addendum: we do have a standard DPA exhibit for onshore routing carve-outs. I am sharing a draft DocuSign link for your procurement team to review. If FinVault needs a full exception (SLA change), that requires exec approval; we can provisionally agree to a scoped exception for the pilot with documented mitigations (logging, alerting, and a fall-back plan).

4) Evidence: attached are pointers (SOC2 reports and KMS attestations for EdgeFlow and our telemetry partner). Procurement-grade proofs will be packaged in a compliance binder if you need them for audit intake.

Next steps:
- Sofia will send filtered CSV (finvault_scope) by EOD Mon 11/13.
- We will share the DocuSign DPA addendum link (draft) within 24 hours: https://docusign.example.com/AA12BB34CC
- Technical workaround (EU-only origin fetch) can be toggled for your tenant within 48 hours if you want immediate mitigation during the pilot.

Attachments: egress-map-edgecache-nov2028.png (PNG stub), supporting-attestations-links.txt (plain text stub listing SOC2/KMS URLs).

Thanks — we’ll keep this constrained to the pilot scope unless procurement asks for enterprise-wide changes.

Kimberly Park
Director, Legal & Compliance, Redwood Inference
